The other entry is a paralog, except at RBM39 R109, where a 6-residue peptide differs from RBM39 only at an isobaric I/L and also occurs in CCDC13; near_match_only = every supporting record matches the entry within 2 residues, not exactly (a variant or sequence conflict); arginine_from_position = the evidence of every supporting record covers other arginines of the entry too (a peptide with several arginines, or a window or peptide found more than once): the positions the sources report pick this one (evidence_check agrees_reported_arginine); paralog_assigned = the peptide or window of the site's records occurs once in each of several reviewed entries (shared_with_paralogs), so mass spectrometry cannot tell which carried the methyl group: the site is on the copy most of its records name, the protein the studies assigned the peptide to (the paralog rule); shared_sequence = residues -15 to +15 occur identically in another reviewed entry (same_window_accessions): histone variants, identical paralogs. This version keeps the reported arginine inside the peptide; unreviewed_accession = the previous version filed reviewed-entry numbering under the source's unreviewed or obsolete accession. This version files it under the reviewed entry; lysine_window = the source window is centred on a lysine. The previous version turned it into a nearby arginine site; truncated_window = the window is cut short at a protein end. The previous version read it as if centred, taking the arginine at or nearest the middle of the short window. This version counts from its intact end; multi_arginine_peptide = a peptide with several arginines that does not cover the reported position. The previous version guessed one; peptide_start = a peptide with several arginines, numbered differently from the entry. The previous version took the arginine nearest its middle. This version counts the reported position from the peptide's start in Maron 2021 Tables S2/S3; wrong_protein = the previous version filed the position under another reviewed protein than the one whose sequence matched; outdated_accession_or_symbol = the source accession is merged or obsolete, or its gene symbol outdated. This version reaches the current entry; entry_not_in_reference = no reviewed entry has the source accession or gene symbol (an entry deleted from Swiss-Prot, a readthrough or an unreviewed entry). The evidence occurs once in the reviewed proteome, and this version places it there. For the deleted duplicate genes CBSL, OVOS2 and SIK1B that is the paralog holding the same sequence (CBS, OVOS1, SIK1); evidence_mismatch = the previous version kept the reported arginine although the source peptide or window does not match the entry there; window_padding = the window is padded where it runs off a protein end. The padding now gives the cut side; ambiguous_evidence = the evidence supports several sites equally. This version leaves the record unplaced; one_sided_window = the site is kept pending a decision (flag one_sided_window); reference_renumbered = the same residue under a new number: UniProt 2026_03 extends the sequence at the N-terminus (RAB12, +96); new_record = a source record this version reads for the first time (a study table read for the first time) supports the site; not_localised = the source gives nothing that localises the methyl group to one residue (a compiled record, or a study without localisation scores whose peptide leaves several residues): this version places only localised records; not_unique_in_proteome = a localised record whose evidence names several sites in the reviewed proteome, one site in a protein the record does not name, or none: this version places such records only where the evidence is unequivocal; other = placement changed for a reason not covered by the codes above

A set is tested when it has at least one methylated member and its size is within the analysis's range; fisher = two-sided Fisher exact test (scipy), q = Benjamini-Hochberg within the analysis and method.
